purpose: Register authoritative candidate data sources that could eventually support cohort-level life-path model calibration, validation, or external comparison. This registry does not grant access, download data, or prove model validity.

currentBoundary.summary: The registry only maps possible data sources to future model roles and governance constraints.

minimumUseRequirements: Confirm access rules and data-use agreement before any acquisition.
Define target population, time zero, outcomes, censoring and predictors before using any source.
Record missingness, measurement error, representativeness and linkage limitations.
Use a held-out or external validation design before making predictive-validity claims.
Keep all outputs cohort-level and prohibit individual death-date prediction.

candidates.name: Health and Retirement Study
candidates.populationFrame: Representative U.S. aging panel; HRS describes approximately 20,000 surveyed people in America.
candidates.ageFrame: Older adults and spouses; aging-focused population.
candidates.governanceStatus: Requires HRS data conditions of use; restricted and administrative linkages require separate approval.
strengths: Aging-specific longitudinal design.
Strong resource, work, retirement, health and cognition variables.
Useful for effective-time and future-option-value proxy design.
limitations: Not a full biomedical biomarker platform for all participants.
Restricted data and administrative linkages require governance.
U.S. aging-panel transportability must be tested before broader use.
prohibitedClaims: Does not prove Human Infra model calibration.
Does not support individual death-date prediction.
Does not by itself prove causal intervention effects.

candidates.name: NCHS Linked Mortality Files for NHANES and NHIS
candidates.populationFrame: NCHS survey participants linked to National Death Index mortality follow-up.
candidates.ageFrame: Survey-specific; public-use mortality files contain limited adult mortality data.
candidates.governanceStatus: Public files are privacy-protected; restricted-use files require NCHS Research Data Center approval.
strengths: Direct mortality follow-up through NDI linkage.
NHANES adds examination, laboratory and biomarker measurements.
Useful for testing mortality associations and biomarker proxy boundaries.
limitations: Public-use mortality variables are limited and may be privacy-perturbed.
Not designed as a repeated individual life-course panel in the same way as aging panel studies.
Restricted variables require formal application.
prohibitedClaims: Does not provide individual predictions.
Does not prove Human Infra model calibration.
Does not convert biomarker associations into causal intervention effects.

candidates.name: UK Biobank
candidates.governanceStatus: Researchers must go through UK Biobank approval and use the restricted cloud-based platform.
strengths: Large prospective dataset with rich genetic, phenotypic and health record dimensions.
Useful for high-dimensional predictor and biomarker validation stress tests.
Strong external validation candidate for UK middle-aged-to-older population.
limitations: Access is restricted and governance-heavy.
Participant selection and UK-specific transportability must be assessed.
Privacy and data security risks must be handled as first-class constraints.
prohibitedClaims: Does not authorize local data use without approval.
Does not make the Human Infra model calibrated.
Does not justify individual longevity or health decisions.

candidates.name: NIH All of Us Research Program
candidates.populationFrame: NIH precision-medicine cohort intended to include a diverse U.S. participant base.
candidates.ageFrame: Broad adult and participant program frame; exact analysis cohort must be defined per study.
candidates.governanceStatus: Requires approved researcher access and program data-use rules.
strengths: Designed for broad precision-medicine research and underrepresented groups.
Potential bridge between EHR, surveys, genomics and participant-provided information.
Useful for transportability and equity checks.
limitations: Outcome definitions depend on available EHR and survey coverage.
Mortality and long-horizon effective-time outcomes require careful endpoint review.
Cannot be treated as accessed or usable without governed workspace approval.
prohibitedClaims: Does not prove model fairness or representativeness by itself.
Does not permit local data extraction here.
Does not prove Human Infra model calibration.
Does not support individual prediction claims.

candidates.name: National Health and Aging Trends Study
candidates.populationFrame: Nationally representative sample of Medicare beneficiaries ages 65 and older.
candidates.governanceStatus: Use requires following NHATS data access and citation rules.
strengths: Directly targets functioning in later life.
Annual interviews support effective-time and disability-trajectory thinking.
Good candidate for function-weighted survival model validation.
limitations: Focused on older Medicare beneficiaries, not full adult life course.
Biomarker depth is not the main strength.
Transportability outside U.S. older adults requires external comparison.
prohibitedClaims: Does not represent younger adult trajectories.
Does not prove Human Infra model calibration.
Does not prove biomedical intervention effects.
Does not support individual-level decisions.

candidates.name: English Longitudinal Study of Ageing
candidates.populationFrame: Representative English population aged 50 and older.
candidates.governanceStatus: Use governed by ELSA / UK Data Service access conditions and study documentation.
strengths: Aging panel with health, social, wellbeing and economic circumstances.
Useful for validating resource and social-support variables outside the U.S.
Sister-study relationship helps compare aging panel designs.
limitations: Country-specific system and policy context.
Data access and linkage fields must be checked per release.
Not a standalone biomedical deep phenotyping platform.
prohibitedClaims: Does not prove global transportability.
Does not prove Human Infra model calibration.
Does not validate individual predictions.
Does not replace source-specific governance review.

candidates.name: Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe
candidates.populationFrame: Longitudinal data from Europeans aged 50+ across many countries.
candidates.governanceStatus: Use governed by SHARE ERIC access and non-commercial research terms.
strengths: Cross-national design supports transportability checks.
Combines health, biomarkers, cognition, employment, social networks and economics.
Useful for separating biological signals from policy and social-support contexts.
limitations: Cross-country harmonization and missingness must be handled explicitly.
Endpoint availability and follow-up depth vary by wave and country.
Non-commercial access terms constrain use.
prohibitedClaims: Does not prove one model transports across all countries.
Does not prove Human Infra model calibration.
Does not allow commercial or coercive scoring.
Does not support individual longevity prediction.

candidates.name: Framingham Heart Study
candidates.ageFrame: Multiple cohorts; original cohort began with adult participants.
candidates.governanceStatus: Access depends on study, data repository and consent restrictions.
strengths: Longitudinal risk-factor tradition with deep cardiovascular history.
Useful for checking classical risk modeling and biomarker-to-outcome logic.
Multigenerational structure can inform long-run cohort design.
limitations: Original population is geographically and demographically specific.
Cardiovascular strength does not cover all Human Infra outcomes.
Modern effective-time, AI and resource variables may require other sources.
prohibitedClaims: Does not validate broad effective-immortality claims.
Does not cover all aging mechanisms.
Does not prove Human Infra model calibration.
Does not support individual death-date prediction.

nextWork: Convert each candidate into a Source Card with access rules, variable dictionaries and endpoint definitions.
Select one development-candidate and two external-validation candidates before any calibration attempt.
Write a data-card template covering missingness, representativeness, linkage, measurement error and governance.
Keep this registry candidate-only until a governed data acquisition plan exists.
